{
  "hook": "Xinomavro from Naoussa always walks a tightrope between Barolo perfume and sun-baked Greek herbs; Ramnista plants its vines on the appellation’s higher, south-facing marl terraces, so the wine keeps that perfume but lands with a darker, ferrous punch.",
  "wine_summary": "Kir Yianni owns 58 ha on the southeastern lip of Naoussa, where the Vermio mountain foothills push the vineyard zone above 300 m. That altitude keeps acids bright in Xinomavro, a variety that can taste tomato-skin bitter when grown lower and warmer. The estate farms gravelly clay-limestone plots first mapped by Bordeaux consultants in the late 1990s; the same soils that give structure also force yields down to 40 hl/ha, so Ramnista routinely clocks 14% alcohol yet feels leaner than Barolo at 13.5%. In Greece the wine is benchmark: it shows up on every Athens wine-bar list priced under €30, and exports arrive in quantities large enough to keep U.S. retail below $30 even after two years in 30% new French barriques.",
  "terroir_expression": "Marl interlayered with calcareous sandstone drains quickly on these slopes; water stress concentrates Xinomavro’s pyrazines, so the wine carries green olive and dried-oregano top-notes that read distinctly Mediterranean. Cold air sliding down the Vermio range at night locks in malic acid, meaning Ramnista hits 6 g/l TA even in hot years, translating to that mouth-watering cut that keeps the tannins from turning gritty on the finish.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-sorted berries ferment in 10-ton open stainless steel with twice-daily pigeage for 18-20 days; the cap stays submerged just enough to avoid over-extraction of Xinomavro’s seed tannins. After malolactic in tank the wine ages 18 months in barrique (30% new) then 12 months in bottle before release, a timeline that sands down the variety’s fierce tannins but leaves the tell-tale tomato-leaf savor.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken sandwich: the wine’s high acid and ferrous bite reset the palate between cayenne waves. Lamb ribs with mountain oregano rub: herbal echo plus tannin to chew through char. Spit-roasted pork belly and tzatziki: fat softens tannin, acid cuts garlic. Fine-dining: braised goat over hilopytes pasta – tomato-cinnamon sauce mirrors the wine’s dried-herb lift. Aged, oily graviera cheese: umami amplifies leather notes, tannin scrubs the sheep-milk butterfat.",
  "comparable_wines": "Burlotto Langhe Nebbiolo 2020 – same acid spine, tarry florals, $10 more. Château Oumsiyat St John Mourvèdre 2019 – Bekaa Valley limestone gives similar iron/rust edge, half the price. Paolo Bea Barbaresco 2018 – comparable tomato-leaf savouriness, needs longer cellaring, +$20.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-plus bodied dry red with firm tannins and tomato-herb savor",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2017-2027; earlier for fruit, later for leather-truffle development. Keep below 14°C; Xinomavro’s acid keeps corks from drying but heat dulls the aromatics fast.",
  "value_assessment": "$29 lands Ramnista between Langhe Nebbiolo at $24 and entry Barolo at $45. For that middle ground you get Nebbiolo perfume, Greek price, and a house style already aged three years post-barrique. It outruns similarly priced Etna Nerello which lacks Xinomavro’s tannic grip.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers Greek by-the-glass programs rely on Ramnista because it can pour two days open without fading; collectors see it as weekday Barolo insurance; casual shoppers grab it when Burgundy creeps past $35.",
  "insider_take": "Skip Ramnista if you want immediate plush fruit – the wine always opens with a hard tannic snap that needs protein or time. Buy it when you want Nebbiolo aromatics without the Piedmont tariff, and accept that the mid-palate will stay lean; that’s the site talking, not a flaw.",
  "aging_potential_years": 12,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 4,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,
  "sensory": {

    "color_intensity": "medium",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",

  }
}
